Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}

text:
This looks like the post-COVID recovery. Unemployment is 10.2%, which fits October 2020 (October 2020 was 6.9%, so it does not fit). Unemployment was 10.2% in the data as of August 2020 (8.4%) or in July 2020 (10.2%), so July 2020 fits best.

Checking the other figures against July 2020:
- Industrial production was about -8% YoY, consistent with July 2020.
- Payrolls averaged +3.1 million over three months, consistent with May–July 2020.
- CPI was 1.0% YoY, consistent with July 2020.
- The 10-year yield was 0.55–0.74%. At July's end it was about 0.53%, which is somewhat below the 0.74 shown. The 10y-2y spread of 0.60 is also off for July, when it was about 0.45.

The unemployment rate looks like the July reading, but the yields look closer to August. At the end of August 2020 the 10-year was about 0.70% and the 2-year about 0.13%. That fits the snapshot's 0.74 and 0.14, with a spread of 0.60. August 2020 returns also fit: US equities gained about 7% in the month, and the 20+ year Treasuries fell about 5%. The unemployment figure of 10.2% would be the July reading, still the latest published at that time, since August's was released in September.

The VIX of 22.96 matches the end of August 2020 (about 26), roughly. The snapshot matches August 2020 overall.
